item.dc:creator: Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Trump Tries a New Press Secretary With Midterm Problems Mounting
item.description: Katia Zacharia, the president’s new press secretary, will have to tout his record to voters unhappy with their cost of living.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: KKR Partner Alisa Wood Sees Record Year in Private Equity Exits
item.description: Alisa Wood, partner at investment company KKR, said that her firm has broken its previous record for asset sales because it is 'linear' in how it exists businesses and doesn't wait for businesses to reach the IPO market before selling. Speaking to Bloomberg's Dani Burger at the CAIS Summit in Beverly Hills, Wood commented on the crowded private equity landscape and said that there are too many funds, potentially limiting smaller managers ability to grow value. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trumps Heads To Alaska For Sullivan Rally
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss President Donald Trump's trip to Alaska. On today's show, Stimson Center Senior Fellow Kelly Grieco, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Morning Consult US Political Analyst Eli Yokley. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed's Williams Says One More Rate Hike This Year Is Appropriate
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams says one more interest-rate hike is appropriate this year, but he doesn't think the central bank will have to raise rates again in 2027. Williams spoke to Bloomberg off camera in New York. Bloomberg's Michael McKee reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dems More Motivated to Turn Out in Midterms Than Trump Base, Says Eli Yokley
item.description: Eli Yokley, politics analyst for Morning Consult, said that race ratings are turning away from Republicans because Democrats are more motivated to turn out to vote in the upcoming midterm elections than the Trump base. Yokley said Trump's approval rating has declined significantly in key states like Alaska and Kansas as war with Iran drags on. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Needs To Navigate DC Power Shifts: Brummer
item.description: Chris Brummer, CEO of The Fintech Foundation, joins Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the upcoming US midterms, prediction markets, and US regulation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Anxiety Collides With the Midterms
item.description: Artificial Intelligence anxiety is moving from Silicon Valley into the political arena ahead of the midterm elections. Concerns that began with jobs and the enormous sums pouring into AI have spread to increasingly powerful models, with some industry leaders calling for stronger guardrails. Ed Ludlow looks at how those fears are colliding with Washington’s push to maintain America’s AI lead. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Is Trump’s Diesel Deal With Russia Legal? US Sanctions Explained
item.description: With his Republican Party facing the prospect of losing control of Congress in Nov. 3 elections, President Donald Trump has sought ways to tame a significant source of voter discontent: elevated fuel costs. Saying that lower prices for Americans were his “greatest priority,” Trump announced via social media on Oct. 9 that he’d struck a deal with President Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply the US and global market with diesel. item.dc:creator: Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: US to Use Cold War-Era Law to Expand Delek Refinery in Texas
item.description: Vice President JD Vance announced plans by the administration to work with Delek US Holdings Inc. to expand a refinery in Texas, the latest effort to tout energy investments to lower fuel prices ahead of November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Lucia Kassai

item.title: New Hampshire GOP Senate Candidate Blasts Trump on Iran, Russia
item.description: Republican John Sununu criticized President Donald Trump’s handling of the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict in the first debate in an unexpectedly close New Hampshire US Senate race.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ryan

item.title: Trump Faces Growing GOP Revolt Over His Russian Diesel Deal
item.description: President Donald Trump confronts growing opposition within his own party to his deal with Vladimir Putin on Moscow’s exports of diesel, reached just weeks after he signed a law authorizing stiff sanctions on countries that buy Russian oil.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: GOP Super PAC Cuts Funds to New Jersey’s Kean Ahead of Midterms
item.description: The Republican super political action committee aligned with House Speaker Mike Johnson is cutting funding to Republicans in four key races as it seeks to shore up candidates elsewhere ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: India-US Trade Talks Heading in Right Direction, Jaishankar Says
item.description: Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar says trade talks with the US are heading in the right direction, but he doesn't want to "spill the beans." He speaks with Bloomberg News Editor-in-Chief John Micklethwait at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India's Jaishankar Says China Not Giving Level Playing Field
item.description: Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar says India and China are discussing whether they can settle some parts of their disputed border before reaching a deal on the entire boundary during an interview with Bloomberg Editor-In-Chief John Micklethwait at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Senate Republicans Pouring $8 Million More Into Nebraska Race
item.description: The Senate Republicans’ allied super political action committee plans to spend an additional $8 million to aid embattled Nebraska Senator Pete Ricketts who faces a strong challenge from independent Dan Osborn.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: White House Says Ambassador Guilfoyle Was Asked to Resign
item.description: The White House said it has asked US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign from her post following allegations of unethical conduct.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and Viktoria Dendrinou

item.title: Tourist Hotspot Mauritius Declares Curfew After Riots
item.description: Prime Minister Navinchandra Ramgoolam of Mauritius, an Indian-ocean island nation best known for its white-sand beach resorts, declared a curfew after the worst riots since 1999.
item.dc:creator: Kamlesh Bhuckory

item.title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts New Houthi Missile Attacks on Riyadh
item.description: Saudi Arabia intercepted more missiles and drones launched by Yemen’s Houthis on Tuesday, as fighting with the Iran-backed militant group showed few signs of subsiding.
item.dc:creator: Christine Burke

item.title: French Student Protests Enter 3rd Week as Budget Talks Start
item.description: French high school students hit the streets again on Tuesday, extending their movement into a third week with no clear response from policymakers to their demands in sight.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot and Ania Nussbaum
